brief: One drawer and one spike, both at the very same corner of the same cell, touching.

requirements.requirement: One drawer and one spike, both at the very same corner of the same cell, touching
requirements.evidence: Build now is 3× full pieces at 0,0,0 0,1,0 1,0,0 with no spike and no drawer (get_build, check_build meshClash clear, no errors). Tested configuration: spike only offered at junction 0,0|0,1|1,0 (find_sockets spike s97) where three cells meet; notch drawer only offered in outward empty pockets -1,1(k0), 1,-1(k4), 1,1(k2) – e.g. notch:0#1,1#notch2 (hex-drawer-frame-notch-mf). When both placed (spike:0#0,0|0,1|1,0 + notch drawer at 1,1 k2) the spike sits at the central triangle corner of cell 0,0,0 while the notch occupies the opposite empty hex bridging 0,1,0-1,0,0 and its closest point is the far end of the shared edge 0,1,0|1,0,0 – one edge-length away, not touching at same corner. No socket combination exists where a notch (needs empty spot beside two touching bases) and a spike (needs three cells meeting) coincide at the same corner of the same full cell; cut-face drawers (family drawer) require half bases and yielded zero sockets in this full-base build, and cannot share a corner spike without mesh/placement clash.

finish.summary: Build fails brief: no drawer+spike can be made to share the very same cell corner touching – configurator geometry separates spike junctions (inside triangle of three cells) from notch-drawer pockets (outside that triangle) by one edge. Current build left as stable 3-cell L for inspection, verified clear.
